categories.name: Rapid Assessment and Triage
categories.description: Short, fast-tracked patient encounters consisting strictly of initial registration, triage, and basic blood work or diagnostics without admission or intensive intervention, resulting in quick release or completion within minutes.
categories.rationale: Groups low-duration, low-length variants where patients undergo immediate screening and initial diagnostic labs (CRP, Leucocytes) and are resolved rapidly.

categories.name: Acute Emergency Treatment
categories.description: Patient paths that involve immediate stabilization via IV fluids and IV antibiotics following triage and lab work, representing acute medical management within the emergency setting.
categories.rationale: Characterized by moderate duration and intermediate trace lengths where administration of IV fluids and antibiotics is the core intervention.

categories.name: Inpatient Admission and Recovery
categories.description: Encounters requiring formal hospital admission (NC or IC) following initial emergency stabilization and diagnostics, ultimately culminating in a successful discharge or release category.
categories.rationale: Captured by variants showing transition from ER activities to ward admissions (Admission NC/IC) and subsequent releases (Release A, B, C, D).

categories.name: Chronic Rework and Readmission
categories.description: Complex, highly prolonged variants featuring extensive repetition of diagnostic tests (CRP, Leucocytes, LacticAcid) and ward readmissions, frequently ending in a return to the emergency room or prolonged stays spanning months.
categories.rationale: Clearly separated by extreme duration (up to hundreds of days), massive trace lengths, and explicit rework flags on diagnostic activities.
